resources.string: Termux: BFU
Termux: BFU

BFU mode uses device-protected storage before the first unlock. With pre-authorized Magisk root it starts Debian 13 systemd as PID 1 in private mount, PID, UTS, and cgroup namespaces. The Samsung 4.4 compatibility path keeps Android IPC and network namespaces and remains running after USER_UNLOCKED. Never place passwords, tokens, or private keys in BFU storage.

Migrating from the BFU-enabled Termux:Boot build: stop Debian and disable Direct Boot in the old app before enabling this app. Both apps share /data/local/debian but have separate supervisors, UIDs, settings, and Device Protected Storage. Grant Magisk root and provision authorized keys again here.

Unsafe: allow BFU when this app’s CE storage is readable

Leave this disabled on correctly configured FBE devices. Enable it only when the BFU sentinel proves this ROM exposes CE before first unlock and you accept that platform-level risk. It never bypasses encryption; it only permits Debian startup after recording a warning.
BFU SSH authorized keys (Device Protected Storage). Paste bare public-key lines only. Key options, passwords, private keys, and tokens are rejected or forbidden.

Rootfs installation runs only after unlock. In Termux, first run: pkg install debootstrap util-linux mount-utils. The app downloads pinned official Debian artifacts, verifies SHA-256, and builds a staging tree before publishing /data/local/debian.

Enable Direct Boot Debian bootstrap before installing.
Unlock Android before installing the Debian rootfs.
Install Debian 13 Trixie rootfs?

This downloads Debian 13 Trixie packages and runs upstream debootstrap as pre-authorized Magisk root. Existing /data/local/debian is never overwritten or upgraded in place. Keep this app open to watch the live log.

After the Trixie rootfs install succeeds, this AFU-only step installs systemd, D-Bus, and OpenSSH. It creates user debian, copies the validated DE public keys, disables password/root login, enables ssh.service on TCP 22, masks Android-host-sensitive units, and writes the BFU-ready marker only after validation.
Configure Debian 13 systemd + SSH

Configure Debian systemd and SSH?

This temporarily stops a running BFU Debian instance, uses apt inside /data/local/debian, and then starts the configured system again for validation. SSH accepts only the public keys shown above. Keep this app open to watch the live log.

Debian starts automatically during LOCKED_BOOT_COMPLETED after all BFU gates pass. USER_UNLOCKED never stops or restarts it. Start, restart, and status also verify systemd PID 1, D-Bus, ssh.service, and TCP 22; results are persisted in the DE log.

Stop BFU Debian?
This explicitly asks the Debian container service manager to exit gracefully and stops SSH. Unlock events do not perform this action.

Restart BFU Debian?
This gracefully exits the verified Debian PID 1, starts a fresh isolated instance, then waits for D-Bus, SSH, and TCP 22 health checks. USER_UNLOCKED never performs this action.

Local Debian account passwords (AFU only). Values are sent directly to Debian chpasswd and are never saved in Android preferences, BFU storage, or logs. SSH remains public-key-only. Setting the root password allows “su root” inside Debian and grants device-level root authority; use a unique strong password.
